customManagers.description: The .NET SDK pinned in mise (Renovate's mise manager does not update dotnet); comment lines may sit above it
The extra .NET runtime pinned in mise (Renovate's mise manager ignores the runtime element)

packageRules.description: The samples consume this repository's own packages at the local 0.0.0-sample placeholder that build/pack.proj packs; never bump them to a published release (ignorePaths alone has not kept Renovate out of the sample csproj files)
The per-Roslyn-version analyzer builds pin their dependencies on purpose
The extra runtime is the net10.0 test runtime; the SDK carries the newest one

Ship the .NET SDK (global.json and mise.toml) and the extra runtime in the same PR as the NuGet packages: the 11.0 prerelease packages need the runtime that SDK carries, and the org preset's dotnet/runtime rule would split the runtime into its own patch PR

net10.0 assets stay on the 10.0.x release train; the net11.0 group moves along 11.0.x. Serilog.Extensions.Logging versions with Microsoft.Extensions.Logging (11.x needs Logging 11 on every target framework)
The Aspire CLI pinned in mise resolves the AppHost builds' bundle (ASPIRE009) and pairs with the Aspire.Hosting.* package version, so it moves in the same PR as them

Shipped: src/Joinery.Dovetail.ModularPipelines builds on ModularPipelines, and the Dovetail SDKs pin it and Microsoft.Azure.Functions.Worker into the Packages.props they ship. The org preset marks them private; this repository ships them
Only the tests, samples and Sdk.Tests scaffolds use these: consumers of this repository's packages never get them
